title: Unique stagewise integer shifts with identity-normalized inclusions
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and an arbitrary scheme $Y$. The universe of $Y$ and the universe of $\Omega$ are independent. Let $I$ be the directed poset of finite coefficient subfields of $\Omega$ [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Use the specified small coefficient models, intrinsic raw rational stages $C_E=D^b_c(Y,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and the datum-free normalized scalar stage system $S$ of [lem-general-algebraically-closed-coefficient-stages]. Write $T_{EL}$ for its transition for $E\le L$, $a_{ELM}:T_{LM}T_{EL}\cong T_{EM}$ for its associator, and $\sigma_{EL,n,K}:T_{EL}(K[n])\cong(T_{EL}K)[n]$ for its fixed integral-image-normalized integer-shift comparison. Let $P=S.\mathrm{PairCategory}$ be the category with literal objects $(E,K)$ and morphisms the classes $[L,u]$ modulo equality after common-stage transport [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. Write $j_E:C_E\to P$ for the specified inclusion. No finite-field datum, geometric base-field structure, noetherian assumption, or Karoubi completion is part of this construction.

Give $P$ the abelian-group Hom structure determined by the actual directed colimit [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups, lem-pur-general-pair-hom-coordinates]. There exists exactly one full coherent integer-shift structure $s$ on this fixed category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with the following properties. Every shift functor is additive, and for every $n\in\mathbf Z$ its object map is literally
$$ (E,K)[n]=(E,K[n]). $$
For every representative $[L,u]:(E,K)\to(F,H)$ it has the formula
$$ [L,u][n]=[L,\sigma_{FL,n,H}^{-1}\circ u[n]\circ\sigma_{EL,n,K}]. $$
The formula is interpreted after the displayed object equalities, equivalently by heterogeneous equality as in the recorded declaration. There exist coherent comparisons $\beta_{E,n,K}:j_E(K[n])\cong(j_EK)[n]$ making every $j_E$ commute with all integer shifts, whose hom components are the identity of the displayed shifted pair. The zero and addition equations are those of coherent shift-commuting functors: the degree-zero comparison is the one induced by the two shift-zero isomorphisms, and the comparison at $n+m$ is the composite induced by those at $n,m$ and the two shift-add isomorphisms. Uniqueness is equality of the entire $\mathrm{HasShift}$ structure, including its shift-zero and shift-add coherence data, not merely equality of the functors. The existential inclusion comparisons are constrained to the stated identity components; they are not arbitrary exactness witnesses.

source.note: Construction material for GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.shift_existsUnique: shift every finite representative by the prescribed sigma conjugation. Scalar associator compatibility makes this independent of stage and respects identities/composition. Descend the stagewise shift-zero and shift-add components; their diagrams hold at a common finite stage. The colimit sum formula gives additive shifts. Stage inclusion comparisons have identity components on literal shifted pairs. These components and the CommShift zero/add equations force the zero/add isomorphisms at every pair; since every object is a pair, uniqueness concerns the entire HasShift structure. This preserves the full coherence argument rather than only equality of the functors.

proof.text:
By [lem-pur-intrinsic-associator-shift-square], the actual intrinsic associators satisfy
$$\sigma_{EM,n,K}\circ a_{ELM,K[n]}=a_{ELM,K}[n]\circ\sigma_{LM,n,T_{EL}K}\circ T_{LM}(\sigma_{EL,n,K}).$$
Thus for each integer $n$ the functors $\Phi_E=[n]$ and comparisons $b_{EL}=\sigma_{EL,n}$ satisfy exactly the tower equation of [lem-pur-unnormalized-pair-functor-descent]. All indices, including repetitions, are allowed; no identity normalization of $T_{EE}$ is used.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-unnormalized-pair-functor-descent] to this family for every integer $n$. It gives a functor $Q_n:P\to P$ with the literal object and representative formulas in the statement, and $Q_nj_E=j_E[n]$ on objects and arrows. Thus the inclusion comparison has identity components. For two arrows choose a common stage using [lem-pur-general-pair-hom-coordinates]. At that stage the formula for $Q_n$ is the additive map $u\mapsto\sigma_F^{-1}u[n]\sigma_E$: additivity of the stage shift and bilinearity distribute it over $u+v$, and it sends $0$ to $0$. The cited Hom-coordinate formulas $[L,u]+[L,v]=[L,u+v]$ and $[L,0]=0$ show that every $Q_n$ is additive for exactly the specified group laws.

proof.text:
Write $z^E_K:K[0]\cong K$ and $c^E_{n,m,K}:K[n+m]\cong(K[n])[m]$ for the given stage coherence. Their families are compatible transformations: the compatibility equations with a transition are precisely its CommShift zero and addition equations, supplied by [lem-general-algebraically-closed-coefficient-stages]. Apply [lem-pur-unnormalized-pair-functor-descent] to them and to their inverses. Identity/composition descent identifies their targets with $\operatorname{id}_P$ and $Q_mQ_n$, giving natural isomorphisms
$$z_{(E,K)}=j_E(z^E_K),\qquad c_{n,m,(E,K)}=j_E(c^E_{n,m,K}).$$
For example the associativity equality at $(E,K)$ is $Q_d(c_{n,m,(E,K)})c_{n+m,d,(E,K)}=c_{m,d,Q_n(E,K)}c_{n,m+d,(E,K)}$; substitution of the displayed components and $Q_dj_E=j_E[d]$ makes both sides $j_E$ of the stage associativity equality. The two unit equalities similarly become $c_{0,n,(E,K)}=Q_n(z_{(E,K)}^{-1})$ and $c_{n,0,(E,K)}=z_{Q_n(E,K)}^{-1}$, by applying $j_E$ to the stage unit equations. The core construction [lem-pur-coherent-shift-from-core] therefore gives a full HasShift structure with these precise functors and isomorphisms.

proof.text: Give $j_E$ the identity comparison $\beta_{E,n,K}$. It is natural because $Q_nj_E=j_E[n]$ from [lem-pur-unnormalized-pair-functor-descent]. Its zero equation reduces to $z_{j_EK}=j_E(z^E_K)$, and its addition equation reduces to $c_{n,m,j_EK}=j_E(c^E_{n,m,K})$; these are exactly the components constructed in the preceding step. Thus these are coherent inclusion comparisons, rather than a freely chosen family of exactness witnesses.

proof.text: For uniqueness take any two structures satisfying the stated conditions and identify their object maps by the required equalities. Every arrow is a representative by [lem-pur-general-pair-hom-coordinates], so the representative formula identifies their arrow maps, hence each $Q_n$. With identity inclusion comparisons, the inclusion CommShift zero equation forces $z_{(E,K)}=j_E(z^E_K)$, and its addition equation forces $c_{n,m,(E,K)}=j_E(c^E_{n,m,K})$. Every object is literally $(E,K)$ [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data], so the two natural isomorphisms agree everywhere. In the definition of HasShift as a monoidal functor, the functor on the discrete category is fixed by the $Q_n$ (its maps are forced by identities); its monoidal unit and tensorator are the inverses of $z$ and $c$. Inverses of isomorphisms are unique, and the remaining fields are proofs of equations. Thus the whole HasShift structures are equal, including the zero and addition data. The existential inclusion witnesses add no choice, since their hom components have already been forced to be identities.

lean.statement:
theorem shift_existsUnique :
    ∃! s : HasShift (Pair l Ω Y) ℤ,
      (fun [shiftInst : HasShift (Pair l Ω Y) ℤ] ↦
        (∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor (Pair l Ω Y) n).Additive) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (A : Pair l Ω Y),
          (shiftFunctor (Pair l Ω Y) n).obj A = shiftPair n A) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (A B : Pair l Ω Y) (L : Index l Ω)
          (hA : A.stage ≤ L) (hB : B.stage ≤ L) (f : StageHom A B ⟨L, hA, hB⟩),
          HEq ((shiftFunctor (Pair l Ω Y) n).map (ofHom A B L hA hB f))
            (ofHom (shiftPair n A) (shiftPair n B) L hA hB
              (shiftRepresentative n A B L hA hB f))) ∧
        ∃ c : ∀ E : Index l Ω, (inclusion E : Stage l Ω Y E ⥤ _).CommShift ℤ,
          (fun [commInst : ∀ E : Index l Ω,
              (inclusion E : Stage l Ω Y E ⥤ _).CommShift ℤ] ↦
            ∀ (n : ℤ) (E : Index l Ω) (K : Stage l Ω Y E),
              HEq (((inclusion E : Stage l Ω Y E ⥤ _).commShiftIso n).hom.app K)
                (𝟙 ((inclusion E : Stage l Ω Y E ⥤ _).obj
                  ((shiftFunctor (Stage l Ω Y E) n).obj K)))) (commInst := c))
        (shiftInst := s)
